name: VoiceStudio.sh
tagline: Make voices. Tell stories. Keep the files.
description: Clone, design, dub, dictate, and build audiobooks in one open-source desktop studio. Local-first by default — no subscription, no usage meter; online services stay opt-in.
audience: Creators, localization teams, and developers who need a serious voice workflow without renting every second of it from a hosted API.
positioning: Your Voice. Your Hardware. Your Studio.

features.title: Own the Voice Pipeline
features.description: Clone, design, generate, dub, and dictate from one desktop studio, with the models and output under your control.

features.title: Move from Clip to Production
features.description: A multi-track dubbing workflow, audiobook editor, project library, voice gallery, and engine controls turn isolated model demos into repeatable work.

features.title: Run Where the Work Lives
features.description: Use MLX on Apple silicon, CUDA on NVIDIA, ROCm on Linux, Docker on a server — or the OpenAI-compatible API from another tool.

tables.heading: The Scoreboard
tables.lead: Same jobs, different terms. This is the table that made me build it.
rows: Gender, age, accent, pitch, style, dialect
Fork it, extend it, ship it

tables.heading: The System Floor
tables.lead: A GPU is optional. The whole pipeline runs on CPU — slower, but yours.
rows: NVIDIA CUDA · Apple MPS · AMD ROCm (Linux)

tables.heading: Sixteen Voices In, Eleven Ears Out
tables.lead: One picker, Cmd/Ctrl+E from anywhere. Defaults are chosen; the rest auto-detect or install on first use.
rows: CosyVoice 3 · VoxCPM2 · IndexTTS 2.5 · MLX-Audio on Apple Silicon
Parakeet TDT at ~10× realtime on CPU · FunASR with inline diarization
tables.footnote: Drop-in OpenAI/ElevenLabs-compatible API: point your existing SDK at localhost — voice takes your own cloned-profile IDs, model pins an engine per request.
